caption: US President Barack Obama throws out the first pitch at the 2009 MLB AllStar Game at Busch Stadium on July 14 2009 in St Louis Missouri

evidences.title: St Louis, Missouri, 14 July 2009 | Barack Obama | The Guardian
evidences.content:
He might be able to swat flies in his sleep, charm the world's most intransigent leaders, take 10 impossible decisions before breakfast and even make the Queen laugh, but here was the real test: could the world's most famous man throw a baseball?

When Barack Obama threw the ceremonial opening pitch at the Major League All-Star game in St Louis, Missouri, he was doing more than throwing a five-ounce sphere of rubber wrapped in white leather. He was following the likes of Franklin Roosevelt and Kennedy to become the fifth president, and the first in 33 years, to open this game, and doing so, of course, in times of unparalleled media scrutiny. Much, much more than a simple throw.

When George W Bush opened for the New York Yankees in 2001 just weeks after 9/11, it was seen as a vital boost to morale. He threw a pretty good pitch; the crowd leapt and chanted: "USA! USA!" A celebrated episode of The West Wing was built around debate by spin-doctors over whether President Bartlet, after terrorist threats, should wear body armour for his pitch. Cincinnati mayor Mark Mallory survives only by a hair after a woeful local pitch in 2007 missed by more than 30 feet: the video has been laughed at 2 million times on YouTube.

Last week's Obama critics were split. Most described the pitch, a soft, high ball that just reached the catcher, as adequate or workmanlike if a little, shall we say, dainty. Liberals pointed out in mitigation that his own sport is basketball. But some bloggers denounced the pitch as "unAmerican" and shock-jock Rush Limbaugh declared that Obama "throws like a girl", whereas Bush had acquitted himself like a man. Acceptance from the right will only come, surely, when Obama manages to fall off a Segway, choke on a pretzel and start a few unwinnable wars.
